name: L'Annuaire des Entreprises
description: L’Annuaire des Entreprises is the French government’s official search interface for legal information on companies, associations and public administrations. It resolves an entity to its SIREN and SIRET identifiers and presents data drawn from other administrations, including the Registre National des Entreprises and the Base Sirene, rather than holding a register of its own.

publicAccess.notes: The service is published as a free official search interface. The overall access posture was not exercised, so the level stays unknown.

bestFor: Resolving a French business name to its SIREN or SIRET identifier free of charge.
Getting an overview of an entity from several official sources before going to the originating register.
notRecommendedFor: Use as the legal source of record, which remains the Registre National des Entreprises, the Base Sirene or the other originating registers.
Obtaining a certified extract, which is issued by the originating register rather than by this interface.
pros: It is free to consult and is published by the French government as the official search interface for business information.
It resolves an entity to its SIREN and SIRET identifiers, which is what most French administrative processes key on.
It brings data from several administrations together in one place, including the Registre National des Entreprises, the Base Sirene and the Bulletin officiel des annonces civiles et commerciales.
The data it uses is published openly, so the same sources can be obtained directly rather than only through the interface.
cons: It is a consultation interface, not the legal source of record. The registers it draws on — the Registre National des Entreprises and the Base Sirene among them — remain the authoritative sources, and a legal question belongs to them.
Because it presents data assembled from several administrations, a discrepancy is resolved against the originating register rather than against this interface.
The interface is French-language.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-04; source-of-record corrected 2026-08-05 (Wave 1D). CORRECTION: this record previously carried primaryRegistryType business-entity-register and described the service as a directory "publishing official legal information", which read as a claim to be the register. It is not. The service publishes itself as the official search engine, and its own data-sources page states that it uses the data of different administrations, all of it openly downloadable, listing among the sources the Registre National des Entreprises and the Base Sirene des Entreprises alongside BODACC and others. Reclassified to corporate-number-database, whose boundary note covers exactly this case: an identifier lookup is not automatically the legal register of the entity, and where the identifier is issued by a statistical body while incorporation happens elsewhere the record takes this type rather than company-register. Operator is unchanged and remains correct. Score unchanged: the interface is as useful and as trustworthy as before, and only its described legal role was wrong.

name: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle
description: French state institute maintaining the national business register alongside trademark, patent and design registers.
nativeName: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle

operator.name: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI)

pros: Operates the Registre national des entreprises
Single-window system for business formalities
cons: Fees apply to some filings; pricing not established from the homepage
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-04. The RNE has replaced the traditional Kbis system.

name: Registre national des entreprises
description: Registre national des entreprises is the French national business register instituted by the Commercial Code and kept by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle. Since 2023 it records every business operating in France, whatever its legal form, replacing several separate registers that previously covered traders, craftspeople and agricultural businesses.

operator.name: Institut national de la propriété industrielle

publicAccess.notes: The data portal refused automated requests during verification and its search behaviour was never observed, so no access fact is claimed and no search URL is published.

bestFor: Establishing that a business operating in France is entered in the national business register, whatever its legal form.
Understanding which single register replaced the older separate registers for traders, craftspeople and agricultural businesses.
notRecommendedFor: Resolving a SIREN or SIRET identifier, which is the Sirene register kept by the statistical institute.
Assuming a particular access or fee position, because the portal refused verification and none is claimed here.
pros: It is instituted by the Commercial Code as the national business register, so an entry reflects a statutory registration rather than a listing.
It covers businesses of every legal form in one register, replacing several that previously ran in parallel.
Keeping it is assigned by statute to a named public body rather than left to an administrative arrangement.
cons: The data portal refused automated verification, so whether search is free, whether an account is needed and what a result contains are all unestablished here.
It does not assign the SIREN and SIRET identifiers, which come from the Sirene register kept by the statistical institute.
It is a register of businesses. It establishes nothing about solvency, licensing or conduct.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-05 from the Commercial Code and official INPI sources. FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: Code de commerce, the section on the registre national des entreprises: article L123-36 institutes the register, and article L123-50 assigns the keeping of it. The register is the constitutive national record of businesses operating in France. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Institut national de la propriété industrielle, named in the Commercial Code as the body that keeps the register. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: Not separately identified from any official page fetched. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The INPI data portal at data.inpi.fr. Its behaviour was NOT observed: the host refused automated requests during verification, so every access field stays null and no search URL is published. Kept deliberately separate from the already-published fr-inpi record, which points at inpi.fr and covers the institute’s intellectual-property registers. Kept separate too from fr-annuaire-entreprises, which is a consultation interface over this register and others and is not itself a register — the distinction corrected in the previous wave.

name: Répertoire Sirene
description: Répertoire Sirene is the French identification register kept by the national statistics institute, which assigns the SIREN number to a business and the SIRET number to each of its establishments. It identifies and describes businesses and their establishments; it does not constitute their legal existence.

operator.name: Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques

publicAccess.notes: The institute’s documentation was read directly and open data derived from the register is published, but no interactive public search surface was exercised, so the search and fee position stays unestablished.

bestFor: Understanding what the SIREN and SIRET identifiers are and which body assigns them.
Reaching the open data published from the French business identification register.
notRecommendedFor: Establishing that a business legally exists, which is the national business register rather than this identification register.
Assuming a live search is available on this address, because none was exercised during verification.
recommendedIndustries: Businesses and establishments identified in France
pros: It is the authoritative source of the SIREN and SIRET identifiers, which nearly every French administrative process keys on.
It covers establishments as well as businesses, which the legal registers do not.
Data derived from it is published as open data, so it is reusable rather than only consultable.
cons: It is an identification register. Being recorded in it does not establish that a business legally exists — that is the national business register.
No interactive public search surface was exercised during verification, so the search and fee position is not established here.
It is maintained for identification and statistical purposes, so it should not be read as a statement about a business’s standing or activity.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-05 from the statistics institute’s own documentation. FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: The register is instituted in the regulatory part of the Code de commerce. It is an identification and statistical register: it does not constitute a business’s legal existence, which since 2023 is the function of the registre national des entreprises. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques, which manages the register. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: Not separately identified from any official page fetched. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: Documentation and open data published on insee.fr. No interactive search surface was exercised, so the access level is recorded as partially-open on the strength of published open data alone, with every boolean left null. Classified corporate-number-database, matching the type’s boundary note exactly: where the identifier is issued by a statistical body while the constitutive registration happens elsewhere, the record takes this type rather than company-register. The website field points at the institute’s own documentation page rather than at a search surface, because no search surface was verified.

name: BODACC
description: BODACC is the French official bulletin that gives publicity to acts recorded in the national business register. It publishes registrations, modifications, transfers, removals, insolvency and conciliation proceedings and notices that company accounts have been filed, together with certain civil announcements.
officialName: Bulletin officiel des annonces civiles et commerciales
nativeName: Bulletin officiel des annonces civiles et commerciales
englishName: Official Bulletin of Civil and Commercial Announcements

operator.name: Direction de l’information légale et administrative

publicAccess.notes: The bulletin’s pages were retrieved anonymously with no credential and no fee, and the site states that its contents are published under the open etalab-2.0 licence unless stated otherwise. The separate account host used for the alert subscription service returned a JavaScript interstitial and was not exercised, so nothing is asserted about it.

bestFor: Reading the official announcement of a French company’s registration, modification, transfer or removal, with its publication date.
Following French insolvency and conciliation proceedings as they are announced, and seeing which companies have filed accounts.
notRecommendedFor: Treating the bulletin as the register itself. It publishes acts recorded in the national business register; it does not constitute them.
Retrieving filed documents such as articles of association or annual accounts, which it announces but does not carry.
recommendedIndustries: French registered businesses and their counterparties
pros: It is the national bulletin of record for French commercial announcements, so a publication in it is the official publicity of the underlying act rather than a report of it.
Its own pages state where the data comes from — the public registers of the commercial court registries and the other courts named there — which makes the chain from court to bulletin explicit.
The data is published as open data under the etalab-2.0 licence, so it can be reused without negotiating access.
cons: It carries announcements, not the documents themselves. A notice that accounts have been filed is not the accounts.
It is a publication medium rather than a register, so a search here answers what was announced and when, not what the register currently says.
The alert subscription service sits on a separate host that returned a JavaScript interstitial to automated requests, so its behaviour is not documented here.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-05 from the bulletin’s own about and legal-notice pages. This record exists partly to make an access-versus-source distinction explicit, which is the acceptance criterion this wave was published against. FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: The acts are recorded elsewhere. The bulletin’s own about page states that it gives publicity to acts registered in the registre national des entreprises, and that the information published about registered businesses comes from the public registers of the commercial court registries, the proximity and judicial courts, the overseas mixed commercial courts, the courts of first instance and the courts of appeal. Civil announcements are transmitted by the civil court registries, notaries, court-appointed agents and the Banque de France over-indebtedness commissions. The bulletin is the publication medium; it constitutes nothing. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Direction de l’information légale et administrative, a service of the Prime Minister, named on the legal-notice page as the publisher of the site and described on the about page as the editor of the bulletin. The directrice de la publication is named there as an individual and is deliberately not recorded in the operator field, which identifies an office rather than an officeholder. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: Opendatasoft, with hosting listed alongside Outscale. The legal-notice page names both as hosting providers, and the site is served as an Opendatasoft data portal. Neither is the responsible authority. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The public site at bodacc.fr, which carries the announcement search and the open data and API route. An API section exists but its navigation entry is hidden by the site’s own stylesheet, so it is not described here as a visible section. Registry type: public-filing-database, on the vocabulary’s own inclusion note that the content is filed documents — accounts, notices, statements, announcements. insolvency-register was considered and rejected: the bulletin announces insolvency proceedings but the boundary note requires the register to hold the proceedings, which the courts do. company-register and business-entity-register were rejected outright, because treating a bulletin as a register is exactly the error this dataset corrected for Germany, France and Spain in an earlier wave.

name: REGAFI
description: REGAFI is the French register of financial firms authorised to operate in France, published by the prudential supervisor. It is served from one portal together with REFASSU, the corresponding insurance register, so a single search surface covers both populations.

operator.name: Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution

publicAccess.notes: The portal was retrieved anonymously and identifies its operator in its own page title, but the search itself is a client-rendered application that was not exercised, so no search behaviour is asserted and no search URL is published. The portal advertises an API, which was not exercised either: an API is not evidence of public interface behaviour.

bestFor: Checking whether a financial firm is authorised to operate in France, and under which category.
Reaching the French prudential supervisor’s own record of an authorised firm rather than a commercial copy.
notRecommendedFor: Checking insurance, banking or finance intermediaries, who are registered separately in the intermediaries register rather than here.
Treating authorisation as a statement about a firm’s solvency, conduct or the suitability of its products.
recommendedIndustries: Financial firms authorised to operate in France
pros: It is the prudential supervisor’s own register, so an entry is the authoritative record of authorisation rather than a directory’s claim of it.
One portal serves both the financial and the insurance register, so a user does not have to know in advance which applies.
The supervisor publishes an API alongside the portal, so the data is reachable programmatically as well as by search.
cons: The search is a client-rendered application that was not exercised, so its behaviour, any fee and any rate limit were not observed and none is asserted.
It records authorisation status. It does not establish that a firm is solvent, well run or suitable for a given customer.
Intermediaries are not here. Their absence from this register proves nothing, because they are registered in a different one.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 by direct fetch of the portal, and re-verified in a separate direct adversarial pass. FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: The authorisation decisions of the French prudential supervisor, taken under the monetary and financial code. The register publishes those decisions; it does not constitute them independently of the supervisory act. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution, named in the portal’s own page title. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: Not separately established. The portal is served from its own host; no external supplier is named on any page fetched. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The REGAFI/REFASSU portal, which serves both registers from one search surface, together with a published API. Scoping decision, taken deliberately: REGAFI and REFASSU are ONE portal serving two populations, and the portal titles itself as such. They are published as one record rather than two, because splitting a single coherent search system by the population filter it offers would be splitting on a filter rather than on a system. The API and the public interface are the same system and are not published separately for the same reason. Registry type: financial-services-register, whose definition covers firms authorised for regulated financial activity.

name: ORIAS
description: ORIAS keeps the French official register of insurance, banking and finance intermediaries. Registration on it is compulsory, and the body that keeps it operates under the supervision of the Treasury directorate of the economy ministry.
officialName: Registre unique des intermédiaires en assurance, banque et finance
nativeName: Organisme pour le registre unique des intermédiaires en assurance, banque et finance
englishName: Single register of insurance, banking and finance intermediaries

operator.name: Organisme pour le registre unique des intermédiaires en assurance, banque et finance

publicAccess.notes: The site was retrieved anonymously and describes its own role and legal supervision on the page reached, but the search is a client-rendered application that was not exercised, so no search behaviour is asserted and no search URL is published.

bestFor: Checking that an insurance, banking or finance intermediary is registered and therefore permitted to distribute in France.
Distinguishing an intermediary from a directly authorised institution, which is registered elsewhere.
notRecommendedFor: Checking directly authorised financial institutions, which are in the supervisor’s own register rather than this one.
Treating the register keeper as the regulator. It keeps the register under ministerial supervision; it does not supervise the market.
recommendedIndustries: Insurance, banking and finance intermediaries operating in France
pros: Registration is compulsory, so the register is a genuine gate on distribution rather than a voluntary listing.
A single register covers insurance, banking and finance intermediaries together, which would otherwise be three separate checks.
The body states its own legal position plainly, including that it operates under the supervision of the Treasury directorate.
cons: It covers intermediaries only. A directly authorised institution will not be here, and its absence proves nothing about it.
The search is a client-rendered application that was not exercised, so its behaviour and any limits were not observed.
Registration records that an intermediary meets the entry conditions. It is not a statement about how the intermediary advises or behaves.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 by direct fetch, and re-verified in a separate direct adversarial pass. The body’s own words on the page fetched: it is “l’organisme en charge du Registre officiel des intermédiaires en Assurance, Banque et Finance, placé sous la tutelle de la Direction Générale du Trésor (Ministère de l’Economie)”, and “L’immatriculation de ces intermédiaires sur ce Registre est obligatoire.” FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: The official register of intermediaries, kept under French law with compulsory registration. The register is the instrument; the supervisory relationship sits with the state. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: The body charged with keeping the register, operating under the supervision of the Treasury directorate of the economy ministry. This body is deliberately NOT described as the regulator: it keeps an official register under ministerial supervision, and prudential supervision of the market lies elsewhere. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: Not separately established. No external supplier is named on any page fetched. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The public site, which offers an advanced search over the register. Registry type: financial-services-register, whose definition expressly covers firms OR individuals registered to carry on regulated financial activity, and whose boundary note allows a body other than a government agency to operate one. professional-licence-register was considered and rejected: the registered population is intermediaries as businesses and individuals under a financial regime, not a single regulated profession.

name: Tableau des architectes
description: The roll of the French Order of Architects, kept and continuously updated by the regional councils of the Order. Entry on the roll is required to use the title of architect and to carry out the design work reserved to the profession, and the roll distinguishes architects entitled to design work from those registered for other activities.
englishName: Roll of the Order of Architects

operator.name: Conseil national de l’Ordre des architectes

publicAccess.notes: The roll search was served anonymously with no credential, with fields for name, company name or registration number, postcode, town and region of registration, so login is recorded as not required. No query was executed, so result content and any limits were not observed and stay null.

bestFor: Checking that a named architect or architectural company is on the roll of the Order.
Establishing whether an architect is entitled to carry out design and project-supervision work.
notRecommendedFor: Choosing an architect for a project. A separate finder exists for that and is not this register.
Assuming every architect found is insured for design work. The roll states that some are not.
pros: It is the roll of the Order itself, kept continuously up to date by the regional councils rather than compiled periodically.

It separates architects entitled to design, interior and exterior layout, urban planning and works supervision from architects registered for other activities such as teaching, journalism or expert work.
It covers companies as well as individuals, and distinguishes liberal, salaried, associate, public-servant and company modes of practice.
It reaches the overseas regions, including Guadeloupe, Guyane, Martinique and Réunion-Mayotte, not only metropolitan France.
cons: Entry is required both to use the title and to carry out reserved design work, so the two effects coincide here — but an entry is still not a statement about the quality of any project.
Architects registered for other activities are on the roll but are NOT entitled to design work and, as the roll states, are not insured for it. Reading any hit as a designer is an error.
The roll is maintained by the regional councils of the Order, so the national interface aggregates regional decisions and the Order directs doubtful cases back to the regional council.
Several adjacent lists exist beside the roll — holders of a récépissé, service providers, fee lists and a special list of architects’ holding companies — and a search of the roll does not cover them.

Absence from the roll does not establish that a person never practised, and it does not exhaust the Order’s lists. Entry can end, the adjacent lists are searched separately, and the Order directs doubtful cases to the regional council.
No search was executed during verification, so result content and any limits were not observed and none is asserted.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 by navigating from the Order’s own national site to the roll, and re-verified in a separate direct adversarial pass. The roll states: "Le tableau de l’Ordre est mis à jour en permanence par les Conseils régionaux de l’Ordre. En cas d’interrogation ou de doute, consulter le Conseil régional concerné." It distinguishes architects "habilités à exercer des missions de conception, d’aménagement intérieur et extérieur, d’urbanisme, de suivi et d’assistance à la réception des travaux, etc. et sont assurés à ce titre" from architects exercising "une autre activité" of whom it warns "ces architectes ne sont pas habilités à exercer des missions de conception et de maîtrise d’œuvre et ne sont pas assurés à ce titre". Adjacent lists offered beside the roll: "Annexe des détenteurs de récépissé", "Liste des prestataires de services", "Liste des honoraires", "Liste spéciale des SPFPL d’architectes". FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: The roll of the Order, on which entry is decided and maintained by the regional councils of the Order. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Conseil national de l’Ordre des architectes, with the regional councils keeping the roll. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: Not separately established. The roll is served from the Order’s own annuaire.architectes.org domain and no external supplier is named. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The public roll search at annuaire.architectes.org. Duplicate decision, a rejection: architectes-pour-tous.fr ("Trouver un architecte") is NOT this register and was not published. It invites a visitor to "sélectionner des architectes prêts à vous accompagner", filtered by project type, MaPrimeRénov’ referencing and geolocation. That is a client-matching finder operated by the Order, not the roll, and publishing it as a register would publish a marketing directory.

name: Annuaire des experts-comptables
description: The directory of French chartered accountants published by the Order of Chartered Accountants. Its stated purpose is to verify that a professional entrusted with accounting work is an expert-comptable entered on the roll of the Order, which is required because the profession holds an exclusive prerogative over accountancy engagements.

operator.name: Conseil national de l’ordre des experts-comptables

publicAccess.notes: The directory was served anonymously with no credential, with a locality field and a search control, so login is recorded as not required. No query was executed, so result content and any limits were not observed and stay null.

bestFor: Verifying that a person offering to keep your accounts is an expert-comptable entered on the roll.
Establishing that an accountancy engagement is being carried out by someone entitled to it.
notRecommendedFor: Judging the quality of an accountant. The directory records inscription, not performance.
Concluding from absence that a person is not registered. The Order asks readers to report a gap or contact the regional council.
pros: The Order states the directory’s purpose in verification terms — checking that a professional is an expert-comptable inscribed on the roll of the Order.
It makes the exclusive prerogative explicit: accountancy engagements covered by it may be carried out only by an expert-comptable.
It gives a documented route when someone is not found, directing the reader to a reporting form or to the regional council of the Order.
cons: Inscription on the roll is required to carry out reserved accountancy engagements, so this is a licence register — but an entry says nothing about how any engagement was performed.
The Order directs unresolved cases to the regional council, so the national directory reflects decisions taken regionally rather than centrally.
The entry point published by the Order redirects cross-host to a separate directory domain, so a bookmark may not land on the address the reader started from.
The Order presents a figure of 22,000 experts-comptables on the directory itself, which is a headline count rather than a statement that every entry is current at the moment of reading.
No search was executed during verification, so result content and any limits were not observed and none is asserted.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 by navigating from the Order’s own site, and re-verified in a separate direct adversarial pass. The directory states: "La consultation du présent annuaire permet de vérifier que le professionnel à qui vous confiez votre comptabilité est un expert-comptable, et qu’il est à ce titre inscrit au tableau de l’Ordre. Toute mission en lien avec la comptabilité et visée par la prérogative exclusive d’exercice de la profession ne peut être réalisée que par un expert-comptable. A défaut de le trouver dans l’annuaire, remplissez le formulaire de signalement ou prenez contact avec le Conseil de l’Ordre de votre région." FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: Inscription on the roll (tableau) of the Order of Chartered Accountants, decided through the Order’s regional councils. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Conseil national de l’ordre des experts-comptables. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: Not separately established. Served from annuaire.experts-comptables.org, the Order’s own directory domain. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The public directory at annuaire.experts-comptables.org. Redirect note: the Order’s published entry point experts-comptables.fr/annuaire redirects cross-host to annuaire.experts-comptables.org, which is recorded here as the canonical entry and disclosed in the published limitations.

name: Annuaire des conseils en propriété industrielle
description: The directory of French industrial property attorneys published by the INPI, the national industrial property institute. The title of conseil en propriété industrielle is regulated and the list is held by the state institute rather than by the profession’s own trade body.
nativeName: Annuaire des conseils en propriété industrielle

operator.name: Institut national de la propriété industrielle

publicAccess.notes: Result rows were rendered to an anonymous client with no credential and no payment, showing firm name, legal form, address, telephone, email and specialisms, and the page reported 550 results at the time of verification. Free public reading is therefore observed rather than inferred. No filtered query was submitted, so behaviour under a specific search and any rate limit were not observed and stay null.

bestFor: Finding an industrial property attorney recognised by the French national IP institute.
Checking whether a firm holding itself out as a conseil en propriété industrielle appears on the institute’s list.
notRecommendedFor: Assuming the trade body is the register keeper. The list is published by the institute, not by the profession’s national company.
Judging an attorney’s competence in a technology. The list records specialism categories, not proven expertise.
pros: It is published by the INPI itself, the state industrial property institute, rather than by the profession’s own organisation.
Results are readable without an account or payment, which is unusual among the professional registers in this dataset.
It can be narrowed by region and department, including the overseas departments, and by specialism between patents and trade marks, designs and models.
Entries show the practice, its legal form and the number of attorneys attached to it, so a reader sees the firm and its people together.
cons: The title of conseil en propriété industrielle is regulated, but the pages fetched do not establish whether any activity is reserved to the profession. This record therefore makes no claim that inclusion is a licence to practise, and none should be read into it.
The list records firms and the attorneys attached to them, so a result must be read carefully to know whether an individual or a practice has been returned.
Specialism labels distinguish patents from trade marks, designs and models, but they do not establish experience in any particular technology or trade.
The result count shown on entry reflects the unfiltered list at the moment of reading and is not a guaranteed total of the profession.

The list sits on the institute’s main domain alongside its industrial property registers, which are separate systems with a different purpose; a reader arriving from those should not read this as one of them.
Absence does not establish that a person may not advise on industrial property. Attorneys at law and other advisers work in the field without appearing on this list.
editorNotes: Verified 2026-08-06 by navigating from the institute’s own site to the directory, and re-verified in a separate direct adversarial pass. The page is server-rendered and returned result rows to an anonymous client, reporting "550 résultats correspondent à votre recherche" on both the first pass and the adversarial re-check; the figure is recorded as a reading at a moment in time rather than a fixed total. Filters offered: name of attorney or firm, region and department including DOM TOM, and specialism ("Brevets d’invention" / "Marques, dessins & modèles"). FOUR ROLES, determined separately. LEGAL SOURCE OF RECORD: The list of conseils en propriété industrielle held by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle. RESPONSIBLE AUTHORITY: Institut national de la propriété industrielle, the French state industrial property institute. TECHNICAL PLATFORM: Not separately established. Served from the institute’s own www.inpi.fr domain. PUBLIC ACCESS INTERFACE: The public directory at inpi.fr/annuaire-des-conseils. Register-keeper decision: the Compagnie nationale des conseils en propriété industrielle (CNCPI) is the profession’s own national body and is NOT recorded as the register keeper. The institute publishes the directory and is linked from its own resource page about the CNCPI, which is the reverse relationship. Naming a professional organisation as the register keeper is the error corrected for ORIAS in Wave 2A and for the Colegio de Registradores in Wave 1D.  Shared-host note: www.inpi.fr also serves fr-inpi, the institute’s industrial property registers. Both declare resourceIdentity in the inpi-fr group with distinct systemKeys, because a directory of attorneys and a register of industrial property rights are different systems that happen to share a host.

name: Annuaire officiel des notaires de France
description: The official directory of French notaries, published by the notarial profession’s national body. French notaries are public officers appointed to an office, so the directory records who holds a notarial office rather than who has chosen to join a scheme.

publicAccess.notes: The directory was served anonymously with no credential, with separate searches for a notary, an office and a company, plus postcode and town fields, so login is recorded as not required. No query was executed, so result content, coverage and any limits were not observed and stay null.

bestFor: Finding a notarial office in a given town or department, including the overseas territories.
Checking that a named notary or notarial company appears in the profession’s official directory.
notRecommendedFor: Treating an entry as a statement about how a notary performed any act.
Assuming absence means a person is unqualified. Notarial offices are limited in number and a person may hold no office.
pros: It titles itself the official directory of the profession and is published by the profession’s national body.
It searches notaries, offices and companies separately, which matches how the profession is actually organised.
It covers the overseas territories explicitly, including Guyane, Martinique, Guadeloupe, La Réunion, Mayotte and Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon.
cons: It records who holds a notarial office. It is not a statement about how any particular deed or transaction was handled.
French notaries are public officers appointed by the state, so appointment — not entry in this directory — is what confers the office; the directory reflects that appointment.
Optional filters include practical facilities and languages spoken, which are conveniences declared for the office rather than verified statements about a notary’s competence.
No search was executed during verification, so result content, coverage and completeness were not observed and none is asserted.
